facts.statement: Luperosuchus fossils have been found in the Chañares Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: It is known from the Chañares Formation of Argentina

facts.statement: Luperosuchus lived during the latest Ladinian stage of the late Middle Triassic or the earliest Carnian of the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: within strata belonging to the latest Ladinian stage of the late Middle Triassic, or the earliest Carnian of the Late Triassic

facts.statement: Luperosuchus was one of the largest carnivores in the Chañares Formation.
facts.quote: Luperosuchus was one of the largest carnivores of the Chañares Formation

facts.statement: The only known postcranial material for Luperosuchus is a single atlas intercentrum associated with an incomplete skull.
facts.quote: Luperosuchus is known only from a single incomplete skull, with an associated atlas intercentrum representing the only known postcranial material

facts.statement: The preserved portion of the Luperosuchus skull measures 54.5 cm, with an estimated total length of approximately 60 cm.
facts.quote: The skull belongs to a large animal, with the preserved portions measuring 54.5 cm and an estimated complete length of approximately 60 cm

facts.statement: Luperosuchus possesses a tall, mediolaterally compressed crest on the front of its snout.
facts.quote: An unusual feature found in Luperosuchus is the tall, mediolaterally compressed crest that sits on the front of the snout

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PULR 04 was collected by Ruth Romer on January 17, 1965.
facts.quote: The holotype material of Luperosuchus, specimen PULR 04, was collected by Ruth Romer, wife of palaeontologist Alfred S. Romer, on January 17, 1965

facts.statement: Alfred S. Romer published the description of Luperosuchus in 1971.
facts.quote: Romer published his description of Luperosuchus in 1971

facts.statement: Romer originally classified Luperosuchus as a member of the family Rauisuchidae in 1971.
facts.quote: Romer identified Luperosuchus as a member of the family Rauisuchidae in 1971

facts.statement: It is debated whether specimen PULR-V 057 belongs to Luperosuchus or represents a distinct taxon, with some researchers suggesting the differences are taxonomic rather than due to age.
facts.quote: In 2017, the referral of this material to Luperosuchus was questioned by Sterling Nesbitt and Desojo, who suggested that the differences between PULR-V 057 and the holotype of Luperosuchus are taxonomic rather than ontogenetic

facts.statement: The Luperosuchus locality provides a minimum age of 236.1 +/- 0.6 million years.
facts.quote: This would be positioned below the strata recently dated by Marsicano et al., providing a minimum age of 236.1 +/- 0.6 Ma for the Luperosuchus locality

facts.statement: Romer identified fused sutures in the skull of Luperosuchus, suggesting the specimen was mature.
facts.quote: Romer struggled to identify the suture pattern, but identified fused sutures which he interpreted as a possible indicator that the specimen was mature.

facts.statement: Later studies confirmed that the skull bones of Luperosuchus were fully fused and featured well-developed sculpting.
facts.quote: Later examination by Nesbitt & Desojo confirmed that many of the sutures in the skull of Luperosuchus were obliterated, with the bones in the skull fully fused, in addition to well developed sculpting of the bones.

facts.statement: Luperosuchus was one of the largest animals and one of the few large carnivores in the Chañares Formation.
facts.quote: Luperosuchus is one of the largest animals in the Chañares Formation, and indeed was one of the few large carnivores known from the formation.

facts.statement: The early environment of Luperosuchus was a braided river system with periodic flooding.
facts.quote: The early part of the Chañares Formation corresponds to a braided river system with periodic flooding events.

facts.statement: The environment later changed to include volcanic deposits like tuff and ash, indicating regional volcanism.
facts.quote: The environment later shifts to encompass deposits of pyroclastic and volcaniclastic materials, such as tuff and ash, indicating a complex history of regional volcanism in the environment.

facts.statement: The genus Luperosuchus was named by Romer in 1971.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Luperosuchus (genus), Romer 1971

facts.statement: Luperosuchus belongs to the family Rauisuchidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Rauisuchidae

facts.statement: Luperosuchus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Luperosuchus lived during the Ladinian period, between 241.464 and 237 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ladinian to Ladinian (241.464 to 237 million years ago)
